summary: Long Eddy Point, north tip of Grand Manan: 'The Whistle', a steam fog signal from 1874, a 1905 beach fog alarm, and a combined tower from 1966.

structures.type: square reinforced concrete tower combined with fog alarm building

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Coast Guard list gives 'Fl R' with no period printed; OpenStreetMap's 'Fl R 8s' is not followed here because the Coast Guard list is the official source. The period is left unset.
LighthouseFriends gives 1966 for the combined tower and fog alarm building; the record gives 1967. The story uses 1966 and says the record's figure is not confirmed by a source read.
LighthouseFriends gives 2017 for designation under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act; the record gives 2016. Not resolved; the story does not give a designation date.

notes_for_editor: LighthouseFriends is copyrighted and facts-only; the story paraphrases it and keeps quotations short. The Lawson rescue (1857), the 1875 Department report and the 1874 notice are reached only through LighthouseFriends. The Tribune dispatch gives eight men saved, which fits LighthouseFriends' account of Lawson and seven others. The Manlius wreck is dated only to the dispatch (January 1857), not to a day. Tatton is listed by LighthouseFriends as 'Tatton' with the text naming James Tatton as first engineer; the Department table in the report for the year to 30 June 1906 names George T. Tatton on one OCR line (an inline OCR entry on scan p. 180; the page image could not be fetched, so the row alignment is not confirmed by the checker and the page should be read before publication). The 1904 table names him only through a column block that is misaligned in the OCR, so it is not cited. The keeper list runs from 1874; no earlier Department keeper table is in the corpus. Dates conflict: the record gives 1967 for the structure, LighthouseFriends gives 1966 and the story uses it; the Register text read gives no building date, so the record's 1967 is unconfirmed. The 1857 Lawson narrative and the 1857 Manlius detail are from LighthouseFriends and the Tribune only. The heritage date is 2017 in LighthouseFriends and 2016 in the record; not checked against the Register's federal heritage listing 15292. The Coast Guard list prints 'Fl R' with no period, while OpenStreetMap gives 'Fl R 8s' (the record's conflict). Barry Bagley (here 1983 to 1989) is the same name as Barry S. Bagley at Gannet Rock (1989 to 1996); LighthouseFriends does not say they are the same person, so no link is made. Percy Alger Harvey, Willard W. Parker and Barry Bagley are named only as printed, with no further detail.
